cutMap.chipsLabel: Choose a part of the cow

descriptions.neck: A hard-working muscle with plenty of flavour. Best cooked low and slow, or minced.
descriptions.chuck: The shoulder. Rich cuts for braises, stews and mince, plus the oyster blade for the grill.
descriptions.rib: Tender, rich meat from along the back. Home of the ribeye.
descriptions.loin: The most tender part, from along the spine. Striploin and tenderloin come from here.
descriptions.rump: Lean and full of flavour. Good for the grill, lok lak and stir-fries.
descriptions.round: The hindquarter. Lean, versatile cuts for roasting, thin slicing, lok lak and stir-fry.
descriptions.brisket: The chest. Slow cooking makes it tender, for smoking, braising and soups.
descriptions.plate: The belly below the ribs. Flavourful meat for braising and grilling.
descriptions.flank: The lower belly. Long-fibred meat for stir-fries, the grill and mince.
descriptions.fore-shank: The front leg. Full of collagen, it makes rich soups and braises.
descriptions.hind-shank: The back leg. Slow-cooked for deep, rich soups and braises.

story.label: Our story
story.title: Local beef, held to a better standard.
story.p1: BattamBeef starts in Battambang, a province known for its rice fields and farming. Our cattle are raised in Battambang province and processed with a slaughterhouse partner in Battambang.
story.p2: After slaughter, the beef is chilled for 72 hours. It is one step in a simple idea: Cambodian beef can stand with the best when it is handled with care.
story.p3: We are building BattamBeef for the restaurants, food businesses and home cooks who want to know where their beef comes from.

methods.title: Cooking methods
methods.body: Match the method to the cut.

methods.label: Cooking methods
methods.title: Choose a method, find the cut.
methods.cutLink: {cut}: see it on the cut map

guides.grill: High, direct heat for a charred outside and a juicy middle. Pat the meat dry, oil it lightly and let the grill get very hot before you start. Rest the meat for a few minutes before slicing.
guides.pan-sear: A heavy pan, very hot, and not too much in it at once. Sear without moving the meat so it browns, turn it once, and finish with butter if you like.
guides.roast: Steady oven heat for larger pieces. Brown the outside first, roast at a moderate heat, and let the meat rest well before carving.
guides.braise: Brown the meat, then cook it slowly, partly covered in liquid, until it is tender. Hard-working cuts turn soft and rich this way.
guides.stir-fry: Thin slices, a very hot wok and quick cooking. Slice across the grain and cook in small batches, so the beef sears instead of stewing.
guides.soup: Long, gentle simmering draws flavour and body into the broth. Skim the surface early and keep the pot just below a boil.

storage.label: Storage
storage.title: Keep it cold, keep it safe.
storage.body: General food-safety basics for raw beef at home.

fridge.title: In the fridge
fridge.body: Keep raw beef in a fridge at 4°C or colder, never above 5°C. Store it wrapped or in a sealed container on the bottom shelf, so juices cannot drip onto other food.

freezer.title: In the freezer
freezer.body: Freeze at -18°C or colder. Wrap the beef tightly to keep air out, and label it with the date.

thawing.title: Thawing
thawing.body: Thaw frozen beef in the fridge, never at room temperature. Put it on a plate to catch drips and allow plenty of time: large pieces can take a day or more.

refreezing.title: Refreezing
refreezing.body: Do not refreeze raw beef once it has thawed. Cook it instead.

lok-lak.title: Beef lok lak
lok-lak.intro: Cambodia's favourite stir-fried beef, served on salad with a lime and pepper dip.

ingredients.beef: 400 g topside, cut into 2 cm cubes
ingredients.sauces: 1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tbsp soy sauce
ingredients.salad: Lettuce, tomato and onion, to serve
ingredients.dip: Juice of 1 lime with black pepper and a pinch of salt, for the dip
ingredients.rice: Steamed rice or a fried egg, to serve

steps.marinate: Mix the beef with the garlic, sauces and sugar. Leave for 20 minutes.
steps.salad: Arrange the lettuce, sliced tomato and onion on plates.
steps.sear: Heat a wok until very hot. Sear the beef in small batches for 2–3 minutes, so it browns rather than steams.
steps.dip: Stir the lime juice, pepper and salt together for the dip.
steps.serve: Pile the beef on the salad and serve with rice and the dip.

pan-seared-ribeye.title: Pan-seared ribeye
pan-seared-ribeye.intro: A thick ribeye with a deep brown crust, basted in garlic butter.

steps.temper: Take the steak out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Pat it dry and season well.
steps.heat: Heat the oil in a heavy pan until it just starts to smoke.
steps.sear: Sear for 3–4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once. Cook longer if you like it more done.
steps.baste: Add the butter, garlic and thyme, and spoon the foaming butter over the steak for a minute.
steps.rest: Rest the steak for 5 minutes, then slice it across the grain.

brisket-soup.title: Slow-cooked brisket soup
brisket-soup.intro: A clear, fragrant broth with brisket simmered until it is soft.

ingredients.aromatics: 1 onion, a thumb of ginger and 2 stalks lemongrass
ingredients.herbs: Spring onion, coriander and lime, to serve

steps.blanch: Blanch the brisket in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse it. This keeps the broth clear.
steps.simmer: Cover with the fresh water, add the aromatics and spices, and simmer gently for 2½–3 hours, until tender.
steps.vegetables: Add the vegetables for the last 30 minutes.
steps.season: Season with fish sauce. Slice the brisket and return it to the pot.
steps.serve: Serve hot with the herbs and lime.

pepper-stir-fry.title: Beef stir-fry with Kampot pepper
pepper-stir-fry.intro: Quick, peppery and made in minutes, with thin slices of flank.

ingredients.beef: 300 g thin flank, thinly sliced across the grain
ingredients.pepper: 1 tsp crushed Kampot black pepper, or fresh green peppercorns
ingredients.sauces: 1 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 tsp soy sauce

steps.slice: Slice the flank thinly across the grain, so it stays tender.
steps.season: Toss the beef with half the sauces and the pepper.
steps.sear: Stir-fry the beef in a very hot wok for 1–2 minutes, then take it out.
steps.vegetables: Stir-fry the garlic and onion, then return the beef with the rest of the sauces and the sugar.
steps.serve: Finish with spring onion and serve with rice.
